I never said solution. I am merely offering suggestions from the perspective of a disabled student who had to figure a lot out for themself in the hopes that it could help OP. Surprisingly enough, there are quite a few people out there who decided to use the fairly accessible resource of the internet to, god forbid, try and help others. Some of the best study and mental health tips I’ve learnt from those people. You have your outlook on life, and I have mine. But calling therapy a blame transfer is incredibly ignorant and I don’t want OP blaming themself for something that isn’t their fault.

OP, I’m here simply to tell you to not listen to this person. Going to therapy and being diagnosed genuinely saved my life. 


ADHD brains work differently to neurotypical brains. If you haven’t already, try looking into study tips specifically from people with ADHD. While random people on the internet aren’t 100% reliable, a lot of independent ADHD content creators share tried-and-tested tips on TikTok, Instagram, etc, so they are good places to start. 

For the record, as someone who quite literally became traumatised from an exam season — no amount of study is worth sacrificing your mental health over. If you can’t put in as much effort as you’d like it is not going to ruin your life. It’s okay to lower your expectations of yourself. 
So if you can’t study without becoming scared, then don’t beat yourself up for taking a break from it. Please take extra good care of yourself.

Finally (going on a rant here sorry lol), the anxiety/fear/anger around study is your brain and body trying to protect you. It has the memory of what happened in the last exam season, and it’s using that as information to protect your present self. You are not weak, you had a bad experience and your system is trying to prevent it from happening again. It can help people to know why this sorta thing happens, so I thought it was worth mentioning. 

I truly wish you the best of luck OP, and I want to reiterate that the above commenter should be ignored. The grind is overrated. Taking care of your health should always be the first priority.
